text: {"question":"How does the neutron lifetime value inferred from primordial helium measurements compare with the average from bottle experiments, and what impact would BBN constraints on the baryon density (Ω_b h^2) have on models that use the helium‑derived lifetime?","reference_answer":"The helium‑derived neutron lifetime is slightly higher than the bottle average, lying around 878–879 s versus the bottle value of 878.3 ± 0.4 s.  BBN constraints on Ω_b h^2, which are tightened by deuterium measurements, would restrict models that rely on the helium‑derived lifetime by limiting the allowed baryon density, potentially ruling out scenarios that otherwise fit the Hubble tension."}
